articles.title: The street fighter who became a cameraman for the kingdom
articles.deck: Pavithran Golconda grew up in a Christian home in Hyderabad and wanted nothing to do with it. He talks about the night that changed him, the band he started, and why he tells beginners to learn on film.

hero.alt: Pavithran Golconda photographed in profile against a dark background

interviewMeta.subject: Pavithran Golconda
interviewMeta.subjectBio: A camera operator with Joyce Meyer Ministries in Hyderabad, and founder of the charity For The People. He plays drums in the band Njavoice.

archiveMeta.editNote: First published as Talent Search #3 under the headline “Miracle Really Happens”. Reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected. One further change: the original described the method of a suicide attempt in detail. That description has been removed, in line with standard safe-messaging practice. Everything else in the account is his, unchanged.

body.v: The story of Pavithran reads like a Christian film, except that it happened. He came through years of anger, depression and loneliness, and when he accepted Jesus his world changed completely. He has kept looking for ways to be used. He shared his testimony with us, and he says plainly: miracles really happen.
The testimony

I grew up in Hyderabad in a Christian home. My family always took me to church but I never wanted to go, and I did not believe anything about the Christian faith. I enjoyed spending time with my friends, smoking and drinking. Eventually I became a street fighter. It got so bad that I had to sign in at the police station every day. My family never knew. I was living in a dark world without peace.

One day I realised that what I was doing was wrong and that I needed to change. There was nobody to counsel me, because people were afraid to talk to me. I was going to church, but my interest was the music and the drums rather than the word of God. I went back to the old life.

People who used to like me started to hate me. Some fought with me. It made me very sad. When I was a bad person I was happy, and when I was doing good things people were hurting me. I was upset and I was depressed.

It got so painful that I went down to a lake and tried to end my life. I began to lose consciousness. I panicked, and the only thing I could instinctively do in my fear was ask God to forgive me. I said: “God, if you save me from death, I will give my life to you and I will share your love with the world.”

God heard that prayer and rescued me. I do not know how it happened, but I found myself in a hospital bed. I woke up and understood that without Him I would not have this second life. I accepted Jesus Christ as my Lord and Saviour.

I went to a fellowship, looking for more of Him. About a year later I gave myself to full-time ministry. We started a band called Njavoice, which goes into villages and shares the love of Jesus Christ with people who have not heard it.
Early in my ministry my father died. God strengthened me through that time.

I founded a charity, For The People, headed by our band pastor Mr Allen. We feed hundreds of people every month, and provide clothing and gifts for those in need. God has blessed me so much that I keep blessing others. But we could not meet the financial need of the ministry, and I had no job. In those days I was helping the church with photography and video. I met Mr Raj, a camera operator from Joyce Meyer Ministries, who supported me and taught me to be a professional cameraman. Later I was hired there as a camera operator. I was so thankful that He had kept His promise. Now I have money to give back to Him, spending it on ministry work.
I knew His name but not His grace. I knew that He was merciful, but now I know His compassion.

Some people call us radicals for Christ, and that is what I am. He rescued me from my sins and gave me a new life. Before, as a Christian, I never understood God’s love. In the past I did not have enough money to travel by city bus; now I am flying on international flights for His glory. In the past I did not have enough money to eat; now I am feeding hundreds of poor children. In the past I knew nothing about running cameras; now I am a professional camera operator and have made many international documentaries. When I was a bad person I hurt a great many people. Now I am sharing God’s love with them.
A conversation with Pavithran
5Talents: How do you usually start your day, in terms of time with God?
I always worship God in my heart. I read the Bible and pray in the morning.
5Talents: How and when did you discover your photography and videography?

I like gadgets and cameras. I found an interest in taking photographs, and that is the talent I discovered in me, given by God to use for His kingdom. I started taking photos and videos at my church, and the leaders and others appreciated them.
5Talents: Did you have special training, or did it come naturally?
The excitement for photography and video was springing up in me. To develop the skills I took support and help from professionals.
5Talents: Is there anyone in particular who helped you stay strong enough to reveal the talent?
I came across Mr Raj, who encouraged me and taught me to become a professional cameraman. I appreciate him for his support.
“Every image has the power to reveal God’s love”
5Talents: In what major ways are you using your talent?

Everything God provides me is His. If I see someone in need, I help them. I am the official magazine photographer of Joyce Meyer Ministries, and since I have been working there I have helped create many documentaries — church updates, church news, testimonies.
5Talents: What has the Lord taught you through your talent?
I hope that my images can express God’s love, or the need for His love.
5Talents: In what ways has God used you to bring blessing to others?

God has given me a heart for those in need. One time a woman with a child came up to me and asked me for money to eat. I only had thirty rupees, so I gave her all of it. She was thankful but confused as to why I would give her all my money when I had not eaten for two days. I told her God will provide for me. Even if I am very hungry I will never leave God, because God is faithful.
5Talents: How much does a Christian organisation need photography and video?

It is very important. There is definitely a need for creative and media people, because they have the power to influence others for God. One testimony has the power to change many lives. Every image has the power to reveal God’s love and glory to the world.
5Talents: You are experienced enough that there are opportunities in the secular world. Why work in Christian services?
I have a passion for Jesus. I am born to serve Him. If my videos can change the lives of those who watch them and make them fall in love with Jesus, why would I want to do anything else?
“Learn on film first”
5Talents: Any advice for people wanting to improve their photography?

First learn basic photography with film cameras, because you will learn good aperture and shutter speed settings. The true photographer knows how to get the best shot manually. Try to take realistic images from nature and you will improve the quality of the image. A good SLR would be best to start.
5Talents: What would you say to someone talented but sad, because they are not given the opportunity, or the talent is not recognised?

Do not worry if your talents are not recognised by others. Give your full effort and do the best work. If you are using your talents for the real purpose, to fulfil God’s will, you will be given opportunities in His due time.
A note from us

This account describes a period of severe depression and a suicide attempt. If any of it is close to where you are now, please talk to someone you trust, or contact a helpline in your country — in India, the Tele-MANAS helpline runs at 14416, free and around the clock.

articles.title: Crossing the Bandra–Worli sea link, I could not see the other end
articles.deck: Five and a half kilometres of cable, thirty thousand vehicles a day, and no way to see where it finishes. A short essay on faith.

archiveMeta.editNote: Lightly edited for reading order and obvious typographical errors. The argument and the voice are unchanged.

body.v: The Bandra–Worli Sea Link is a magnificent piece of engineering: about 5,600 metres long, a cable-stayed bridge with pre-stressed concrete-steel viaducts on either side, linking Bandra and the western suburbs of Mumbai with Worli.

Have you ever travelled on a hanging bridge? The kind that seems to shake to and fro as a heavy vehicle passes, where it is frightening to look down, and where — the funny thing — sometimes you cannot even see the other end.

Last year, on 28 November, I was crossing it. The weather was fine, a cool breeze coming across, the water below clear and blue. I was enjoying the scenery and curious to see where the bridge would end. Then, halfway over, I began to be afraid. Will this bridge be strong enough to hold, with all these cars passing at once? I could not see the other end. It was beyond my vision, and I started to wonder whether I would reach it. I looked at the cables the whole thing hangs from. What if one broke, or lost its grip?

I knew the bridge was only two years old, that thirty thousand vehicles crossed it on an average day, that the construction was planned to last more than a hundred years. I admired the architecture and the design, and inside I still doubted its firmness. I crossed with a little excitement and a lot of anxiety.
The word I kept coming back to

Then I thought for a while about the uncertainties we face every day. It is the same as that bridge hanging across the water, where there is no guarantee of reaching the other end. There will be twists and tilts, ups and downs, sometimes dangerous and worse situations.

Only one word came to me while I was on that bridge, and it was faith. Only complete faith in God would make the journey comfortable and safe. I could not see the other end, and I still believed He would get me there. And He did.
Even where life seems to be a hanging bridge, when we start building faith, uncertain things become certain.

As the Bible says in Hebrews 11:1, “Faith is the confidence that what we hope for will actually happen; it gives us assurance about things we cannot see.” And in 1 Corinthians 16:13, “Be on your guard; stand firm in the faith; be men of courage; be strong.”

This life is full of twists and turns, but there is no need to worry, because God is still working. We come across a great deal of confusion, discouragement, rejection. I want to encourage you to hold on to faith in God in spite of the worst of it. You will see things change, and impossible things turn out to be possible.
Faith allows things to happen. It is the power that comes from a fearless heart. And when a fearless heart believes, miracles happen.

articles.title: You can invest your talent in success, or in something that lasts
articles.deck: The world rewards a hard worker, and it should. But everything built for this world alone has a short life on it.

archiveMeta.editNote: Lightly edited for reading order and typographical errors.

body.v: Today’s world is busy running after success and achievement. Science and technology are two of the things that develop a nation, and we are the ones who put them to use. When we talk about development and success we are also talking about personal development — where we invest our time, our hard work and our talents.

People work hard for their study, their career, their job, and mainly for their own growth, which adds something to the world as well. Parents are glad when their children work day and night to score well. A company wants to hire someone skilled and hard-working. A cricket selection board looks for a good all-rounder. There is nothing wrong with any of it.

Success with science and technology empowers professionals, business and the world, easily and effectively. By investing talent and skill you can become a successful businessman, a leader, a celebrity, a great technologist, a famous singer, a rich man.
For this world alone
But brothers and sisters — what we do here seems great, and it is for this world alone, not for God’s kingdom or His glory. The Bible says everyone has blessings, as gift and as talent.
We have different gifts, according to the grace given to each of us. If your gift is prophesying, then prophesy; if it is serving, then serve; if it is teaching, then teach.
body.highlight: according to the grace given to each of us

body.v: It is amazing that everyone has a blessing from above. Some have found their gifts and some have not. As we read and understand the Bible it becomes necessary to discover and then reveal what is hidden. Those hidden blessings were already granted by God as talent, and they were granted for the purpose of His kingdom.

So the main concern of this life should not be the world’s development but the serving of His kingdom. Everything else under the sun is short-term. “So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.” (2 Corinthians 4:18)
What lasts

Our world is full of unsolved mysteries. Science and technology can go a long way, until they collide with things that cannot be measured. Both the despair of our struggles and the ecstasy of our successes are temporary. So let us keep our eyes on what lasts forever.

God wants us to be successful people in this world for the sake of a kingdom that is eternal. Everyone is blessed with a gift. Our job is to serve with it — as a musician, singer, technician, preacher, prayer warrior, or as a businessman solving the financial needs of ministry work. When we allow ourselves to do that, God is faithful to bless us further and let those talents shine.
“Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, who does not change like shifting shadows.” (James 1:17)

articles.title: “I just came to tell you one thing”
articles.deck: A conversation with God on a wet afternoon, in verse, with the scripture He keeps answering in.

archiveMeta.editNote: Set as verse, with the original line endings kept. Typographical errors corrected; the scripture references are the author’s.

body.v:
One day I was sitting all alone
Kept aside, my dearest phone.
Made myself cozy in my comfort zone,
It was drizzling outside in a sweet musical tone.

I held my hot coffee mug,
Packed myself in my warmest rug.
I sipped my coffee and wished I had someone to share my ecstasy.

I was enjoying the bliss of solitude,
Forgetting for a while the busy multitude.
Watched the rain drops fall on my green lawn,
Then my joy jumped like a young fawn.

A soft gentle voice began speaking to me. It said: aren’t you enjoying these beautiful moments, where you can find time for yourself? You are not drenched in the rain-flooded roads — you are warm indoors.

Then my mind started pondering, and was like,
I am happy for a while,
And when a trouble comes up my tears
overflow like river Nile.

Then I questioned the gentle voice that was speaking to me:
“So which number can I dial in emergency?”
Then the voice swiftly said, 333.
Call to me and I will answer you and tell you great and unsearchable things you do not know.

As I continued, I asked the voice: why do I have to go through so much pain and trouble? Is it true that if we endure the trouble, our strength becomes double? The voice said: I have plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you a hope and a future (Jeremiah 29:11). In all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose (Romans 8:28). Suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope — and hope does not disappoint us (Romans 5:3).

Sometimes I do not understand what is happening in my life. The voice said immediately: be still, and know that I am God (Psalm 46:10). Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight (Proverbs 3:5).
On the guilt
Well — then I feel so guilty when I make a mistake. I am afraid some destruction will come on me.

Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, and now you are living in a period of grace. You are justified freely by his grace (Galatians 3:13). Whoever believes in him is not condemned; the Father sees you through the blood of Jesus (John 3:18). As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us (Psalm 103:12). When God himself is forgiving and forgetting all your sins, why are you still feeling condemned?
That relieved me. I knew it before, but I did not believe it strongly. So you mean that even after so many mistakes and blunders God continues to love me?

Yes, of course. Neither death nor life, neither angels nor demons, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers, neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus (Romans 8:38).
On not being able

Sometimes I feel I do not have the ability to perform. Then I felt as if someone patted me on the shoulder. You might not have the ability others have, but if you are in Christ you have authority over everything. In everything you do you can overflow with excellence, as you are His royal inheritance. You are His legal heir. My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness — in fact you need to say: when I am weak, then I am strong.

Every day you are experiencing His caring touch.
Have you realised how your nails grow each day?
Even if you are walking on rocks and pebbles,
Your strength is renewed like that of an eagle.
Who is doing it?

The food on our plates,
And the passing calendar dates,
The inflated market rates —
Do you think you can handle them on your own?

You carry your phone even to the washroom; have you sensed His presence at least when you groom? Is it so difficult to stay tuned? He neither sleeps nor slumbers. A God who loves even if you do blunders. He cares for you.

Therefore, walk with elegance,
As you have the completed deliverance.
If anyone hurts you, I will take the vengeance.
I don’t expect anything from you, as I know mine is an unconditional love.
Even if you are not faithful, I will be faithful.

I leaned back into my rocking chair and asked the voice: may I know who is speaking? He said, I am the word of God. I just came to tell you one thing. And with a query on my mind I asked Him: what? He said: I love you.

articles.title: Martin Luther promised God he would become a monk, and split the Western church
articles.deck: A miner’s son from Eisleben who was terrified of hell, objected to a fundraising scheme, and translated the New Testament while in hiding.

archiveMeta.editNote: First published in the Missionary Story column. Lightly edited; the two-column reading order has been repaired.

body.v: Martin Luther was born into Roman Catholicism in the small town of Eisleben, near modern Berlin, on 10 November 1483. His parents, Hans and Margarethe, were middle-class peasant labourers. His father, a miner, worked hard to secure a proper education for his son, and by twenty-one Martin held a Master of Arts from the University of Erfurt.

Following his father’s hope that he would become a lawyer, Martin began to study law in 1505. Then a lightning strike narrowly missed him, and in fear for his life he cried out a vow: if he lived, he would become a monk. He entered the Augustinian monastery at Erfurt.

Luther was driven by fear of hell, of God’s wrath, and by a need for assurance about his own salvation. Even after his ordination in 1507 he was haunted by insecurity about his eternal fate, and disillusioned by the immorality and corruption he saw among the priests he visited in Rome.
The birth of the Reformation

As he went deeper into Scripture, and particularly into the letters of Paul, Luther came to the overwhelming conviction that he was saved by grace through faith alone (Ephesians 2:8). When he began teaching biblical theology at the University of Wittenberg, that conviction spilled into his lectures and into his arguments with colleagues. He spoke of Christ as the only mediator between God and man, and of men being justified and forgiven by grace rather than works. Salvation, Luther now held with complete assurance, was a free gift.
It did not take long for the ideas to be noticed. They changed his own life, and they changed the direction of church history.
Salvation is not earned by good deeds but received only as a free gift of God’s grace.
body.attr: The doctrine at the centre of it
body.highlight: received only as a free gift

body.v: The indulgences

In 1514 Luther began serving as a priest at Wittenberg’s Castle Church, and people came to hear the word preached as they had not before. During this time he learned of the practice of selling indulgences. The Pope, drawing at his own discretion on a “treasury of merits from the saints”, sold religious merit in exchange for building funds. Those who bought the documents were promised reduced punishment for their sins, for the sins of dead relatives, and in some cases total forgiveness. Luther objected publicly to the dishonesty of it and to the abuse of church power.

On 31 October 1517 he nailed his ninety-five theses to the university’s notice board — the door of the Castle Church — formally challenging the church’s leaders on indulgences and setting out the biblical doctrine of justification by grace alone. The act has become a defining moment in Christian history, and the symbolic birth of the Protestant Reformation.
Wartburg

In January 1521 Luther was excommunicated. On trial before the highest officials of church and state he was again asked to renounce his views, and again, with nobody able to refute him from Scripture, he stood his ground. His writings were banned and he was declared a convicted heretic. He escaped in a staged “kidnapping” to Wartburg Castle, where friends kept him hidden for almost a year.

During that seclusion he translated the New Testament into German, giving ordinary people the chance to read it for themselves, and Bibles were distributed among the German people for the first time. He died on 18 February 1546.

To some sixteenth-century Christians he was a pioneering defender of truth and religious freedom; to others the heretic leader of a revolt. Most Christians today would agree that he shaped Protestant Christianity more than any other single person.
